title.narrative: TI Indo-Pacific Partnership for Strong, Transparent, Responsive & Open Networks for Good Governance (TI IPP STRONGG)

description.narrative: Project goal: contribute to reduced corruption in the Indo-Pacific region by empowering a resilient and independent civil society voice and network that can mobilise action in support of increased accountability of national and regional public and private institutions. Countries involved are Bangladesh, Cambodia, Fiji, Indonesia, Maldives, Mongolia, Nepal, New Zealand, Pakistan, PNG, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, and Vanuatu.Specific objectives:1. Informed, engaged and local demand for accountability: More people, including women, youth, people with disabilities and socially disadvantaged groups, are actively and collectively engaged in anti-corruption work that results in increased local demand for inclusivity, accountability and transparency. 2. Inclusive, responsive, and accountable governance frameworks: Policies, institutions and enforcement mechanisms relating to good governance are more inclusive, transparent and accountable as a result of greater responsiveness to civic engagement and TI's action. 3. Resilient, independent and active civil society anti-corruption voice across the Indo-Pacific region: TI Movement enhanced capacity to inclusively influence both state and non-state anti-corruption actors. Value of the Australian contract is AUD 14.6 million / EUR 8.75 million. Value of the New Zealand contract is NZD 6 million / EUR 3.3 million. New Zealand contract was active from 1 July 2024.

participating-org.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
New Zealand - Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade - New Zealand Aid Programme

recipient-country.narrative: This project is managed by TI-S which is headquartered in Germany. The countries involved are Bangladesh, Cambodia, Fiji, Indonesia, Maldives, Mongolia, Nepal, New Zealand, Pakistan, PNG, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, and Vanuatu.
